simple.meaning: דְּמָה (dᵉmâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “to resemble.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דְּמָה (H1821) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 3:25, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דְּמָה (H1821) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דְּמָה (H1821) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דְּמָה (dᵉmâh) / H1821 is traced through Daniel 3:25, Daniel 7:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”

timeline.evidenceText: He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”
“Behold, there was another animal, a second, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. They said this to it: ‘Arise! Devour much flesh!’
